```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day goal is one paying customer, and only Idea A has a sourced payer who already pays. Solo therapists pay $49-$99/mo to SimplePractice and $69/mo to TherapyNotes, both cited to the vendors' own pricing pages. Idea B's own brief says every competitor is free or donation-supported, so there is no evidence any user has ever paid for this category.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence points toward a paid product. Sourced therapist complaints say incumbents are 'overkill' and 'really expensive for what it offers,' and a price increase after a 2024 private-equity acquisition is fueling some switching interest. That opens a cheaper option for price-sensitive private-pay solo practitioners. The brief's own caveat that the complaints are about price, not a missing product, weakens but does not remove this opening.",
    "Idea B's case against goes to the core of the business. Fakespot, described as well-funded and Mozilla-backed, shut down in July 2025 instead of sustaining itself. At least five free alternatives sit on the same store listings. Sourced backlash ('downright immoral') shows false positives can damage reputation. Reddit's API terms add platform risk.",
    "Idea A's biggest obstacle is HIPAA compliance, estimated at $8k-$25k in year one with BAAs and audited infrastructure. That is a real cost and timeline risk. It is also a known, purchasable, bounded cost. Idea B's obstacle is market-level unwillingness to pay, which a solo operator cannot buy their way past.",
    "Idea B's price anchor is weak. It uses GPTZero's $10-15/mo writing-detection tier to justify $3-5/mo, but GPTZero is a different use case with a different buyer. No evidence shows Reddit readers paying for filtering."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence is thin and mostly self-referential. Two of the three quotes come from launch threads for builders' own free scripts, and the first is the builder describing his own frustration, not a prospective customer. None of the three indicates willingness to pay. The third is an explicit counter-signal.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Idea A wins mainly on proven willingness to pay in the category. Its own brief undercuts demand for a stripped-down product, and HIPAA overhead could realistically push first revenue past 90 days for one person. Several A data points are unsourced and count as missing: the TheraSoft and TheraFocus prices and the $29 SimplePractice tier. The Upheal switching claim comes from a competitor's blog. Idea B would win only if the goal were users rather than paying customers."
}
```
